sense: a feast or a happy day

evidence: Cic. Arch. 13: fēstōs diēs lūdōrum celebrandōs
terms.comment: Properly “to fill with people”, hence to keep a feast in company (Lewis & Short). It names what is celebrated: nātālem, diem fēstum, nūptiās celebrāre.

terms.gloss: keep, celebrate (a feast day, a birthday)
evidence: Hor. C. 4.11.14: Īdūs tibi sunt agendae
terms.comment: The plain word, with the day as its object.

phrases.latin: Lūcifer ambōrum nātālibus adfuit īdem: ūna celebrāta est per duo lība diēs
phrases.english: the same morning star was there at both our births: one day was celebrated with two cakes (Ovid and his brother, born a year apart)

phrases.latin: dēbēmus mehercule nātālēs tuōs perinde ac nostrōs celebrāre
phrases.english: we really ought to celebrate your birthdays as we do our own

phrases.latin: licet enim sine luxuriā agere fēstum diem
phrases.english: for one can keep a feast day without extravagance

sources: Lewis & Short: celebro · Lewis & Short: ago · Lewis & Short: agito
